content: The University of Worcester is a higher education institution located in Worcester, United Kingdom. It was officially granted university status by the Privy Council in September 2005. Prior to this, it was known as University College Worcester, and earlier as Worcester College of Higher Education. It is the only university serving the counties of Herefordshire and Worcestershire. The institution was originally established in 1947 as part of the University of Birmingham's Department of Education, functioning as an Emergency Teacher Training College. During the 1970s, the Council for National Academic Awards (CNAA) accredited the degrees offered by Worcester College of Higher Education. In 1995, the Herefordshire and Worcestershire College of Nursing and Midwifery was integrated into the institution. By 1997, the Privy Council granted the institution degree-awarding powers, leading to its rebranding as University College Worcester (UCW). In 2005, it achieved full university status. In 2005, the university announced plans to develop a super library in the center of Worcester, which would serve as a combined university and public library—the first of its kind in the United Kingdom. Additionally, a second campus was planned on the site of the former Worcester Royal Infirmary on Castle Street, with construction expected to begin in early 2007. The university also hosts a resident applied theatre company, C&T. The Worcester Students' Union serves as the on-campus union for all students enrolled at the University of Worcester. It provides a variety of facilities, including a shop, offices, a bar called The Dive, a sandwich shop, a lounge area, computer facilities, a Student Advice Bureau, and a Student Development and Welfare Office.
